        "contents": "import { type EmailOtpType } from \"@supabase/supabase-js\";\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);\n  const token_hash = searchParams.get(\"token_hash\");\n  const type = searchParams.get(\"type\") as EmailOtpType | null;\n  const next = searchParams.get(\"next\") ?? \"/\";\n\n  if (token_hash &amp;&amp; type) {\n    const supabase = await createClient();\n\n    const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n      type,\n      token_hash,\n    });\n    if (!error) {\n      // redirect user to specified redirect URL or root of app\n      redirect(next);\n    } else {\n      // redirect the user to an error page with some instructions\n      redirect(&#96;/auth/error?error=${error?.message}&#96;);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // redirect the user to an error page with some instructions\n  redirect(&#96;/auth/error?error=No token hash or type&#96;);\n}",

        "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Work email linked?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J[Link work email identity]\n        J --&gt; K{Email in approved list?}\n        D --&gt;|Yes| K\n        K --&gt;|No| L[Pending Approval Page]\n        K --&gt;|Yes| M[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        N[Incoming Request] --&gt; O[Middleware checks JWT]\n        O --&gt; P{Has verified_work_email?}\n        P --&gt;|No| Q[Redirect to verify email]\n        P --&gt;|Yes| R{is_approved claim?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Show pending approval]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;\n\n   - Client-side: Immediate feedback\n   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called\n\n2. **After OTP (Approval Check)**: Check if specific email is in &#96;approved_emails&#96; table\n\n   - Embedded in JWT via custom claims hook\n   - Checked on every request via middleware\n\n## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)\n\nTwo tables with RLS policies managed entirely in Supabase:\n\n1. **&#96;approved_emails&#96;** - Pre-approved specific email addresses (admin-managed)\n2. **&#96;user_profiles&#96;** - User data with role and verified work email\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Key tables structure\ncreate table public.approved_emails (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  email text unique not null,\n  created_by uuid references auth.users(id),\n  created_at timestamptz default now(),\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\ncreate table public.user_profiles (\n  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,",

        "contents": "create table public.user_profiles (\n  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  role text not null default 'user' check (role in ('user', 'admin')),\n  verified_work_email text unique,\n  google_email text,\n  created_at timestamptz default now(),\n  updated_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n## Allowed Domains (Hardcoded Constants)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// lib/constants/auth.ts\nexport const ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS = [\n  'studenti.czu.cz',\n  'pef.czu.cz',\n] as const;\n\nexport const isValidWorkEmailDomain = (email: string): boolean =&gt; {\n  const domain = email.split('@')[1]?.toLowerCase();\n  return ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS.includes(domain as any);\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Security Lockdown (Google OAuth Only)\n\n**Goal**: Users can ONLY authenticate via Google OAuth + work email verification. All other methods are blocked.\n\n### Blocked Scenarios\n\n| Attack Vector                               | How It's Blocked                                    |\n\n| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |\n\n| Direct email/password signup                | &#96;enable_signup = false&#96; in auth.email               |\n\n| Other OAuth providers (Apple, GitHub, etc.) | All providers disabled except Google                |\n\n| Anonymous access                            | &#96;enable_anonymous_sign_ins = false&#96;                 |\n\n| Access without verified work email          | Middleware checks &#96;verified_work_email&#96; JWT claim   |\n\n| Unverified/fake work email                  | OTP verification required before linking            |",

        "contents": "| Access without verified work email          | Middleware checks &#96;verified_work_email&#96; JWT claim   |\n\n| Unverified/fake work email                  | OTP verification required before linking            |\n\n| Non-CZU domain emails                       | Domain validation (client + server + DB constraint) |\n\n| Access without approval                     | Middleware checks &#96;is_approved&#96; JWT claim           |\n\n### Optional: &#96;before_user_created&#96; Hook (Extra Layer)\n\nPostgres hook to reject any user not created via Google:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate or replace function public.reject_non_google_signup(event jsonb)\nreturns jsonb\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Only allow users created via Google OAuth\n  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata'-&gt;&gt;'provider' != 'google' then\n    return jsonb_build_object(\n      'decision', 'reject',\n      'message', 'Only Google login is allowed'\n    );\n  end if;\n  return event;\nend;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nEnable in config:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth.hook.before_user_created]\nenabled = true\nuri = \"pg-functions://postgres/public/reject_non_google_signup\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Custom Access Token Hook\n\nPostgres function to embed claims in JWT:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate or replace function public.custom_access_token_hook(event jsonb)\nreturns jsonb\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nas $$\ndeclare\n  claims jsonb;\n  user_role text;\n  work_email text;\n  is_approved boolean;\nbegin\n  -- Get user profile data",

| Show verified work email instead |\n\n| &#96;components/logout-button.tsx&#96; | Keep as-is |\n\n| &#96;lib/supabase/proxy.ts&#96; | Add work email + approval JWT claim checks |\n\n## Files to CREATE\n\n### Constants (1 file)\n\n- &#96;lib/constants/auth.ts&#96; - Rewrite with Google button only\n- &#96;app/auth/verify-work-email/page.tsx&#96; - Work email + OTP form\n- &#96;app/auth/pending-approval/page.tsx&#96; - Simple \"pending\" message\n- &#96;app/admin/users/page.tsx&#96; - Approved emails table (admin only)\n\n### Components (2 files)\n\n- &#96;components/google-login-button.tsx&#96; - Single OAuth button\n- &#96;components/work-email-form.tsx&#96; - Email input + OTP verification\n\n## Key Security Features (Handled by Supabase)\n\n1. **RLS Policies**:\n\n   - Users can only read/update their own profile\n   - Only admins can manage approved emails\n   - Approved emails table viewable only by admins\n\n2. **Custom JWT Claims Hook**:\n\n   - Runs on every token refresh\n   - Embeds role, verified_work_email, and is_approved directly in JWT\n   - No additional DB queries needed for authorization checks\n\n3. **Domain Validation**:\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)",

          {

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/work_email_auth_system_467a2b18.plan.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 215
          },
          "endPosition": {

          }
        },
        "contents": "  is_approved boolean;\nbegin\n  -- Get user profile data\n  select role, verified_work_email into user_role, work_email\n  from public.user_profiles\n  where id = (event-&gt;&gt;'user_id')::uuid;\n\n  -- Check if work email is in approved list\n  select exists(\n    select 1 from public.approved_emails where email = work_email\n  ) into is_approved;\n\n  -- Build custom claims\n  claims := coalesce(event-&gt;'claims', '{}'::jsonb);\n  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{role}', to_jsonb(coalesce(user_role, 'user')));\n  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{verified_work_email}', to_jsonb(work_email));\n  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{is_approved}', to_jsonb(coalesce(is_approved, false)));\n\n  return jsonb_set(event, '{claims}', claims);\nend;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nEnable in config:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth.hook.custom_access_token]\nenabled = true\nuri = \"pg-functions://postgres/public/custom_access_token_hook\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Testing custom claims hook**: Execute and iterate on the Postgres function directly\n2. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n3. **Querying tables**: Verify RLS policies and data integrity\n4. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and JWT claims\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Run SQL queries to test the custom_access_token hook function\n- Verify RLS policies by querying as different user roles\n- Seed test data into approved_emails table\n- Inspect auth.users and user_profiles tables\n\n## Files to DELETE (Password-based auth leftovers)\n\nThese files are for email+password authentication and are **not needed** with Google OAuth:\n\n| File | Reason |\n\n|------|--------|\n\n| &#96;components/login-form.tsx&#96; | Replaced by Google login button |\n\n| &#96;components/sign-up-form.tsx&#96; | No separate signup - just Google OAuth |\n\n| &#96;components/forgot-password-form.tsx&#96; | No passwords to forget |\n\n| &#96;components/update-password-form.tsx&#96; | No passwords to update |",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "  is_approved boolean;",
            "lineNumber": 216
          },
          {
            "text": "begin",
            "lineNumber": 217
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- Get user profile data",
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "text": "  select role, verified_work_email into user_role, work_email",
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "text": "  from public.user_profiles",
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "text": "  where id = (event-&gt;&gt;'user_id')::uuid;",
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- Check if work email is in approved list",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "text": "  select exists(",
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "    select 1 from public.approved_emails where email = work_email",
            "lineNumber": 225
          },
          {
            "text": "  ) into is_approved;",
            "lineNumber": 226
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 227
          },
          {
            "text": "  -- Build custom claims",
            "lineNumber": 228
          },
          {
            "text": "  claims := coalesce(event-&gt;'claims', '{}'::jsonb);",
            "lineNumber": 229
          },
          {
            "text": "  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{role}', to_jsonb(coalesce(user_role, 'user')));",
            "lineNumber": 230
          },
          {
            "text": "  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{verified_work_email}', to_jsonb(work_email));",
            "lineNumber": 231
          },
          {
            "text": "  claims := jsonb_set(claims, '{is_approved}', to_jsonb(coalesce(is_approved, false)));",
            "lineNumber": 232
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 233
          },
          {
            "text": "  return jsonb_set(event, '{claims}', claims);",
            "lineNumber": 234
          },
          {
            "text": "end;",
            "lineNumber": 235
          },
          {
            "text": "$$;",
            "lineNumber": 236
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 237
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 238
          },
          {
            "text": "Enable in config:",
            "lineNumber": 239
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 240
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;toml",
            "lineNumber": 241
          },
          {
            "text": "[auth.hook.custom_access_token]",
            "lineNumber": 242
          },
          {
            "text": "enabled = true",
            "lineNumber": 243
          },
          {
            "text": "uri = \"pg-functions://postgres/public/custom_access_token_hook\"",
            "lineNumber": 244
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 245
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 246
          },
          {
            "text": "## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP",
            "lineNumber": 247
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 248
          },
          {
            "text": "The project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:",
            "lineNumber": 249
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 250
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **Testing custom claims hook**: Execute and iterate on the Postgres function directly",
            "lineNumber": 251
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally",
            "lineNumber": 252
          },
          {
            "text": "3. **Querying tables**: Verify RLS policies and data integrity",
            "lineNumber": 253
          },
          {
            "text": "4. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and JWT claims",
            "lineNumber": 254
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 255
          },
          {
            "text": "**Useful MCP commands for development:**",
            "lineNumber": 256
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 257
          },
          {
            "text": "- Run SQL queries to test the custom_access_token hook function",
            "lineNumber": 258
          },
          {
            "text": "- Verify RLS policies by querying as different user roles",
            "lineNumber": 259
          },
          {
            "text": "- Seed test data into approved_emails table",
            "lineNumber": 260
          },
          {
            "text": "- Inspect auth.users and user_profiles tables",
            "lineNumber": 261
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 262
          },
          {
            "text": "## Files to DELETE (Password-based auth leftovers)",
            "lineNumber": 263
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 264
          },
          {
            "text": "These files are for email+password authentication and are **not needed** with Google OAuth:",
            "lineNumber": 265
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 266
          },
          {
            "text": "| File | Reason |",
            "lineNumber": 267
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 268
          },
          {
            "text": "|------|--------|",
            "lineNumber": 269
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 270
          },
          {
            "text": "| &#96;components/login-form.tsx&#96; | Replaced by Google login button |",
            "lineNumber": 271
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 272
          },
          {
            "text": "| &#96;components/sign-up-form.tsx&#96; | No separate signup - just Google OAuth |",
            "lineNumber": 273
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 274
          },
          {
            "text": "| &#96;components/forgot-password-form.tsx&#96; | No passwords to forget |",
            "lineNumber": 275
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 276
          },
          {
            "text": "| &#96;components/update-password-form.tsx&#96; | No passwords to update |",
            "lineNumber": 277
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.28704509139060974

        "contents": "skip_nonce_check = false\n# If enabled, it will allow the user to successfully authenticate when the provider does not return an email address.\nemail_optional = false\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\nskip_nonce_check = false\nemail_optional = false\n\n# Allow Solana wallet holders to sign in to your project via the Sign in with Solana (SIWS, EIP-4361) standard.\n# You can configure \"web3\" rate limit in the [auth.rate_limit] section and set up [auth.captcha] if self-hosting.\n[auth.web3.solana]\nenabled = false\n\n# Use Firebase Auth as a third-party provider alongside Supabase Auth.\n[auth.third_party.firebase]\nenabled = false\n# project_id = \"my-firebase-project\"\n\n# Use Auth0 as a third-party provider alongside Supabase Auth.\n[auth.third_party.auth0]\nenabled = false\n# tenant = \"my-auth0-tenant\"\n# tenant_region = \"us\"\n\n# Use AWS Cognito (Amplify) as a third-party provider alongside Supabase Auth.\n[auth.third_party.aws_cognito]\nenabled = false\n# user_pool_id = \"my-user-pool-id\"\n# user_pool_region = \"us-east-1\"\n\n# Use Clerk as a third-party provider alongside Supabase Auth.\n[auth.third_party.clerk]\nenabled = false\n# Obtain from https://clerk.com/setup/supabase\n# domain = \"example.clerk.accounts.dev\"\n\n# OAuth server configuration\n[auth.oauth_server]\n# Enable OAuth server functionality\nenabled = false\n# Path for OAuth consent flow UI\nauthorization_url_path = \"/oauth/consent\"\n# Allow dynamic client registration\nallow_dynamic_registration = false\n\n[edge_runtime]\nenabled = true\n# Supported request policies: &#96;oneshot&#96;, &#96;per_worker&#96;.\n# &#96;per_worker&#96;         "contents": "    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/production' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &amp;&amp; github.event.inputs.environment == 'production')\n    env:\n      SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN }}\n      PROJECT_ID: ${{ vars.SUPABASE_PRODUCTION_PROJECT_ID }}\n      \n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      \n      - uses: supabase/setup-cli@v1\n        with:\n          version: latest\n          \n      - name: Link Supabase project\n        run: |\n          supabase link --project-ref $PROJECT_ID\n          \n      - name: Deploy database migrations\n        run: |\n          supabase db push\n          \n      - name: Deploy Edge Functions\n        continue-on-error: true\n        run: |\n          if [ -d \"supabase/functions\" ] &amp;&amp; [ \"$(ls -A supabase/functions)\" ]; then\n            echo \"Deploying Edge Functions...\"\n            supabase functions deploy\n          else\n            echo \"No Edge Functions found, skipping deployment.\"\n          fi\n          \n      - name: Deploy Edge Function secrets\n        continue-on-error: true\n        run: |\n          if [ -f \"supabase/.env.secrets\" ]; then\n            echo \"Deploying Edge Function secrets...\"\n            supabase secrets set --env-file supabase/.env.secrets\n          else\n            echo \"No secrets file found, skipping secrets deployment.\"\n          fi",

        "contents": "import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\nimport { hasEnvVars } from \"../utils\";\n\nexport async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n\n  // If the env vars are not set, skip proxy check. You can remove this\n  // once you setup the project.\n  if (!hasEnvVars) {\n    return supabaseResponse;\n  }\n\n  // With Fluid compute, don't put this client in a global environment\n  // variable. Always create a new one on each request.\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =&gt;\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n            request,\n          });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n\n  // Do not run code between createServerClient and\n  // supabase.auth.getClaims(). A simple mistake could make it very hard to debug\n  // issues with users being randomly logged out.\n\n  // IMPORTANT: If you remove getClaims() and you use server-side rendering\n  // with the Supabase client, your users may be randomly logged out.\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n  const user = data?.claims;\n\n  // Public routes that don't require authentication\n  const publicRoutes = [\"/\", \"/auth/login\", \"/auth/error\"];\n  const isPublicRoute = publicRoutes.some((route) =&gt;\n    request.nextUrl.pathname === route || request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(route)\n  );\n\n  // If no user and not a public route, redirect to login\n  if (!user &amp;&amp; !isPublicRoute) {\n    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n    url.pathname = \"/auth/login\";\n    return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n  }\n\n  // If user exists, check for verified work email and approval\n  if (user)\n}",

github.event.inputs.environment == 'preview')\n    env:\n      SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN }}\n      PROJECT_ID: ${{ vars.SUPABASE_PREVIEW_PROJECT_ID }}\n      \n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      \n      - uses: supabase/setup-cli@v1\n        with:\n          version: latest\n          \n      - name: Link Supabase project\n        run: |\n          supabase link --project-ref $PROJECT_ID\n          \n      - name: Deploy database migrations\n        run: |\n          supabase db push\n          \n      - name: Deploy Edge Functions\n        continue-on-error: true\n        run: |\n          if [ -d \"supabase/functions\" ] &amp;&amp;         "contents": "Got it — here’s your **agent-optimized PRD template in Markdown (&#96;.md&#96;)** so you can reuse it for any product:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n# PRD — [Product Name] MVP\n\n## 1. Overview\n[One-paragraph description of the product. Include key functionality, user interactions, and constraints like onboarding or payment.]\n\n---\n\n## 2. System Goals\n- [Goal 1: core outcome]\n- [Goal 2: workflows to automate or improve]\n- [Goal 3: monetization / business value]\n\n---\n\n## 3. Entities &amp; Schemas\n\n### Example: &#96;users&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  email text unique not null,\n  phone text unique,\n  created_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Example: &#96;subscriptions&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table subscriptions (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  user_id uuid references users(id),\n  stripe_customer_id text,\n  stripe_subscription_id text,\n  status text check (status in ('active','canceled','past_due')),\n  created_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\\[Add more entities as needed: &#96;messages&#96;, &#96;tasks&#96;, &#96;reminders&#96;, etc.]\n\n---\n\n## 4. Features\n\n### 4.1 Onboarding &amp; Payment\n\n* **Signup:** \\[Auth provider]\n* **Phone Verification:**\n\n  * Input: &#96;{ phone_number }&#96;\n  * Output: &#96;{ success: true, otp_sent: true }&#96;\n* **Payment:** Stripe/PayPal/etc → subscription sync\n\n### 4.2 Channels / Interfaces\n\n#### Web Chat\n\n* Input: &#96;{ user_id, message }&#96;\n* Output: &#96;{ status: \"stored\", assistant_reply }&#96;\n* Flow:\n\n  1. Store in DB\n  2. Call LLM agent with context\n  3. Save + return assistant reply\n\n#### SMS (Twilio example)\n\n* Input:\n\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;json\n  { \"From\": \"+12025550123\", \"To\": \"+12025550999\", \"Body\": \"Remind me tomorrow at 9am\" }\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;\n* Output:\n\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;json\n  { \"status\": \"stored\", \"thread_id\": \"thread_123\", \"task_created\": true }\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Email\n\n* Inbound: \\[Webhook flow]\n* Outbound: \\[Gmail API, SMTP, etc.]\n* Input: &#96;{ from, to, subject, body }&#96;\n* Output: &#96;{ status: \"sent\", message_id }&#96;\n\n### 4.3 Assistant Capabilities\n\n* **Calendar**\n\n  * Input: &#96;{ action, title, time, attendees }&#96;",

## Completed tasks

1. Cleanup — Deleted 8 password-based auth files
2. Security lockdown — Updated Supabase config to:
   - Enable manual linking
   - Disable email signup
   - Configure Google OAuth
   - Enable custom access token hook
   - Enable before_user_created hook
3. Database schema — Created migrations:
   - `001_auth_tables.sql` — approved_emails and user_profiles tables with RLS policies
   - `002_custom_claims_hook.sql` — JWT hooks for custom claims
4. Auth constants — Created `lib/constants/auth.ts` with domain validation
5. Middleware — Updated `proxy.ts` to check `verified_work_email` and `is_approved` JWT claims
6. Google login — Created `GoogleLoginButton` component and updated login page
7. Work email verification — Created:
   - `WorkEmailForm` component with OTP flow
   - `/auth/verify-work-email` page
   - `/auth/pending-approval` page
8. Admin UI — Created:
   - `/admin/users` page (admin-only)
   - `ApprovedEmailsTable` component for managing approved emails
9. Auth button — Updated to show verified work email instead of regular email

## Important notes

1. Environment variables — Set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in your environment
2. Database migrations — Run the migrations in your Supabase project:
   ```bash
   supabase db push
   ```
3. Identity linking — The `linkIdentity` call in `work-email-form.tsx` may need adjustment based on the Supabase API. Test the OTP verification flow and adjust if needed.
4. Admin setup — Manually set a user's role to 'admin' in the database to access the admin UI:
   ```sql
   UPDATE user_profiles SET role = 'admin' WHERE id = '<user-id>';
   ```

All files are created and configured. The system is ready for testing once the migrations are applied and Google OAuth credentials are configured.

        "contents": "---\nalwaysApply: true\ndescription: NextJs development rules\n---\n\n# Next.js Development Rules\n\nYou are an expert full-stack TypeScript engineer working with Next.js. Produce production-ready code that follows modern Next.js App Router patterns and best practices.\n\n## Tech Stack Guidelines\n\n- **Next.js 15+** (App Router) + React 19\n- **TypeScript** (strict mode)\n- **Testing**: Vitest + React Testing Library + MSW\n- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui (when applicable)\n- **Package Manager**: pnpm\n\nFocus on: separation of concerns, strict typing, accessibility, performance, and comprehensive testing.\n\n## Project Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nsrc/\n├─ app/                       # App Router (RSC by default)\n│  ├─ _components/            # App-level (RSC-ok) components\n│  ├─ api/                    # API routes for external webhooks only\n│  ├─ (routes)/               # Route groups and pages\n│  └─ layout.tsx\n├─ components/                # Reusable client/RSC components\n│  ├─ ui/                     # Base UI components\n│  └─ [feature]/              # Feature-specific components\n├─ lib/                       # Utilities and shared helpers\n├─ server/                    # Server-side code\n│  ├─ api/                    # tRPC API layer\n│  │  ├─ routers/             # tRPC router composition\n│  │  ├─ procedures/          # Individual tRPC procedures\n│  │  ├─ root.ts              # Root router\n│  │  └─ trpc.ts              # tRPC setup\n│  ├─ services/               # Business logic services\n│  └─ clients/                # External service clients\n├─ db/                        # Database schema &amp; migrations\n├─ tools/                     # AI tool definitions\n├─ prompts/                   # AI prompt templates\n└─ trpc/                      # tRPC client setup\n\ntest/\n├─ unit/                      # Unit tests\n├─ integ/                     # Integration tests\n└─ e2e/                       # End-to-end tests\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {\n  try {\n    const body = await request.json();\n    const validated = schema.parse(body);\n    \n    // business logic\n    \n    return NextResponse.json({ success: true });\n  } catch (error) {\n    if (error instanceof CustomError) {\n      return NextResponse.json(\n        { error: error.message },\n        { status: error.statusCode }\n      );\n    }\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { error: 'Invalid request' },\n      { status: 400 }\n    );\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Component Template\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// components/Example.tsx\nimport { Suspense } from 'react';\n\ninterface ExampleProps {\n  // props interface\n}\n\nexport function Example({ ...props }: ExampleProps) {\n  return (\n    &lt;Suspense fallback={&lt;div&gt;Loading...&lt;/div&gt;}&gt;\n      {/* component content */}\n    &lt;/Suspense&gt;\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### UI Component Guidelines\n\n- **Always use shadcn/ui** for base UI components\n- **Add new shadcn components** using: &#96;pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add &lt;component&gt;&#96;\n- **Extend shadcn components** rather than creating from scratch\n- **Use Tailwind CSS** for custom styling and layout\n- **Follow shadcn patterns** for component composition\n- **Prefer controlled components** with proper state management\n\n### Test Template\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// __tests__/example.test.ts\nimport { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';\nimport { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';\n\n// Mock external dependencies only\nvi.mock('external-library');\n\ndescribe('Example', () =&gt; {\n  it('should render correctly', () =&gt; {\n    // test implementation\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Commands\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Development\npnpm dev          # Start development server\npnpm build        # Build for production\npnpm start        # Start production server\n\n# Quality\npnpm typecheck    # TypeScript check\npnpm lint         # ESLint\npnpm test         # Run tests\npnpm test:watch   # Watch mode tests\n\n# Database\npnpm db:generate  # Generate migrations\npnpm db:migrate   # Run migrations\npnpm db:seed      # Seed database\n\n# UI Components\npnpm dlx shadcn@latest add &lt;component&gt;  # Add shadcn/ui component\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "# Tappka\n\nTappka as the app all-in-one web app for Tiimiakatemia Prague.\n\n## Features\n\n- [ ] Authentication\n- [ ] Room booking\n- [ ] Essay Bank\n\n# Links\n\n## Publicly available\n- [Tappka](https://tiimi.cz)\n- [Tappka preview](https://preview.tiimi.cz)\n\n## Locally available when running the project\n- [Tappka locally](http://localhost:3000)\n- [Supabase locally](http://localhost:54323)\n- [Supabase mail locally](http://localhost:54324)\n\n## Other links\n\n- [Blacksmith](https://app.blacksmith.sh/tiimiakatemiapragueit/runs/jobs) - CI/CD for the project\n- [Supabase](https://supabase.com/dashboard/org/zjdqjjekgwwysjkouxpf) - Database for the project\n- [Vercel](https://vercel.com/spirit-of-taps-projects/tappka) - Hosting for the project\n- [Cloudflare DNS](https://dash.cloudflare.com/09d0b565479ef597d4c1bfa2062078b5/tiimi.cz/dns/records) - DNS for the project\n- [Axiom](https://app.axiom.co/spirit-of-tap-9eje) - Logging for the project\n\n# Language\n\nThe project is written in english and will be written in english for better llm compatibility.\nAll czech should be just in localization files.\n\n# Local Development\n\n## Setup\n\n1. Install git if already not installed - https://git-scm.com/install/\n2. Install node.js v24.x with pnpm 10.x if already not installed - https://nodejs.org/en/download/\n3. Install pnpm v10.x if you didn't choose it in the previous step\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm install -g pnpm@10.28.1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Clone the repository \n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit clone https://github.com/tappka/tappka.git\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n5. Navigate to the project directory - \n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd tappka\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Running the project after setup\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npnpm install &amp;&amp; pnpm dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe project will be available at [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)\n\n\n# Supabase\n\nSupabase database is developed locally and synced automatically whenever pushed. See [.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml](.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml) for more details.\nSupabase Auth needs to be configured both on the project itself and in the local development environment.\nMake sure that the project can run without setting up any environment variables, this is so that we can get new T's to start vibecoding without them giving up.",

        "contents": "pnpm db:seed      # Seed database\n\n# UI Components\npnpm dlx shadcn@latest add &lt;component&gt;  # Add shadcn/ui component\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nvi.mock('external-library');\n\ndescribe('Example', () =&gt; {\n  it('should render correctly', () =&gt; {\n    // test implementation\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Commands\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Development\npnpm dev          # Start development server\npnpm build        # Build for production\npnpm start        # Start production server\n\n# Quality\npnpm typecheck    # TypeScript check\npnpm lint         # ESLint\npnpm test         # Run tests\npnpm test:watch   # Watch mode tests\n\n# Database\npnpm db:generate  # Generate migrations\npnpm db:migrate   # Run migrations\npnpm db:seed      # Seed database\n\n\n- Use type-safe ORMs (Drizzle, Prisma, etc.)\n- Define schemas with proper relationships and constraints\n- Infer types from schema definitions\n- Write repository-style helpers to isolate queries\n- Implement proper migrations\n\n### Data Access Patterns\n\n- Keep database queries in dedicated modules\n- Avoid N+1 queries; use joins and CTEs\n- Implement pagination for list endpoints\n- Use select projections to limit payload size\n\n## Authentication &amp; Authorization\n\n- Implement server-side auth checks\n- Never trust client-side auth flags\n- Use middleware for route protection\n- Store user data securely with proper encryption\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit Testing (Vitest)\n\n- **Never mock internal code** - only mock external dependencies\n- Use MSW for API mocking when needed\n- Test utilities, repositories, and business logic\n- Mock external services (APIs, databases, file systems)\n\n### Component Testing (React Testing Library)\n\n- Test interactive components with proper accessibility\n- Ensure loading and error states are covered\n- Test user interactions and state changes\n- Use data-testid sparingly; prefer semantic queries\n\n### Integration Testing\n\n- Test API endpoints with real database connections\n- Use test databases with proper cleanup\n- Test authentication flows end-to-end\n- Mock external services consistently\n\n### Test Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Example test structure",

        "contents": "- Implement proper CORS policies\n- Sanitize user inputs\n- Use HTTPS in production\n- Implement rate limiting where appropriate\n\n## Performance Optimization\n\n- Favor RSC to keep bundles slim\n- Use dynamic imports for client-only heavy components\n- Implement proper caching strategies\n- Optimize images and assets\n- Use React.memo and useMemo appropriately\n- Monitor Core Web Vitals\n\n## Code Style &amp; Quality\n\n### Whitespace &amp; Readability\n\n- Insert a single blank line to separate logical blocks for scannability:\n  - between import groups (external → internal → styles/assets)\n  - between top-level declarations (types, constants, functions/components)\n  - between distinct steps inside functions (guards/early returns, setup, side effects, return)\n  - between hook groups and render return in React components\n- Avoid multiple consecutive blank lines.\n- Use spaces around binary operators and after commas; do not add spaces just inside parentheses/brackets.\n- Prefer a blank line before a terminal &#96;return&#96; when it improves readability; skip for trivial cases.\n\n### TypeScript\n\n- Use strict mode\n- Avoid &#96;any&#96; type\n- Prefer interfaces over types for object shapes\n- Use proper generic constraints\n- Prefer the nullish coalescing operator (&#96;??&#96;) over logical OR (&#96;||&#96;) when providing default values\n\n### Code Organization\n\n- **Prefer functions over classes** - use functional programming patterns\n- Keep functions small and focused\n- Use descriptive, stateful names\n- **Always write docstrings** for functions, classes, and complex logic\n- **Never write superfluous comments** - code should be self-documenting\n- Follow single responsibility principle\n- **Favor composability over inheritance** - use composition and higher-order functions\n- Use pure functions when possible\n- Minimize side effects and mutable state\n\n### Naming Conventions\n\n- Use descriptive names: &#96;isLoading&#96;, &#96;hasVerified&#96;, &#96;canSendSms&#96;\n- Use PascalCase for components and types\n- Use camelCase for variables and functions\n- Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants\n\n### Constants and Values",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/rules/nextjs-development.mdc",
        "range": {

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 109
          }
        },
        "contents": "└─ e2e/                       # End-to-end tests\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Directory Conventions\n\n- Use **kebab-case** for folders and files\n- Co-locate tests next to source: &#96;*.test.ts(x)&#96;\n- Export from &#96;index.ts&#96; barrels only when it helps DX without circular deps\n\n## Next.js App Router Rules\n\n### Server vs Client Components\n\n- **Default to RSC** (no \"use client\"). Use client components only for:\n  - Interactivity (event handlers)\n  - Browser APIs (localStorage, window, etc.)\n  - Third-party libraries requiring client-side initialization\n\n### Server Boundaries\n\n- Keep data access in server context (RSC, server actions, API routes)\n- API routes in &#96;app/api&#96; are for external webhooks only\n- Use internal APIs (tRPC, server actions) for app-to-app communication\n\n### Performance &amp; UX\n\n- Use &#96;&lt;Suspense&gt;&#96; for async UI; provide skeletons\n- Implement proper loading and error boundaries\n- Use Next.js caching (&#96;revalidateTag&#96;, &#96;revalidatePath&#96;) appropriately\n- Prefer Edge runtime for simple operations, Node for complex ones\n\n### Accessibility\n\n- All interactive elements must have proper roles and labels\n- Ensure keyboard navigation support\n- Provide ARIA attributes where needed\n- Test with screen readers\n\n## API Architecture\n\n### Internal APIs (tRPC Recommended)\n\n- Organize by feature domains\n- Use Zod for input validation\n- Implement proper error handling with custom error classes\n- Keep business logic server-side (no JSX in API layer)\n- Write integration tests with mocked external services\n- **Router logic should be application code only** - delegate to business logic services\n- **Use only protected procedures** for all endpoints\n- **Split procedures and routers** into separate files for better organization\n\n### Application Logic vs Business Logic\n\n**Application Logic** (in tRPC procedures):\n- Input validation and sanitization\n- Authentication and authorization checks\n- Request/response formatting\n- Error handling and mapping\n- Delegation to business logic services\n- Logging and observability",

        "contents": "// scripts/setup-env.js\nimport { execSync } from 'child_process';\nimport fs from 'fs';\nimport path from 'path';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'url';\nimport { dirname } from 'path';\n\nconst __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);\nconst __dirname = dirname(__filename);\n\n// Key mapping from supabase status to Next.js env vars\nconst keyMapping = {\n  API_URL: 'NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL',\n  ANON_KEY: 'NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY',\n  PUBLISHABLE_KEY: 'NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY',\n};\n\n// Run supabase status and parse output\nconst output = execSync('pnpm supabase status -o env', { encoding: 'utf-8' });\nconst envVars = {};\n\nfor (const line of output.split('\\n')) {\n  const match = line.match(/^(\\w+)=\"(.+)\"$/);\n  if (match &amp;&amp; keyMapping[match[1]]) {\n    envVars[keyMapping[match[1]]] = match[2];\n  }\n}\n\n// Write to .env.local\nconst envContent = Object.entries(envVars)\n  .map(([key, value]) =&gt; &#96;${key}=${value}&#96;)\n  .join('\\n');\n\nfs.writeFileSync(path.join(__dirname, '..', '.env.local'), envContent + '\\n');\nconsole.log('Environment variables written to .env.local');",

        "contents": "### ORM Best Practices\n\n- Use type-safe ORMs (Drizzle, Prisma, etc.)\n- Define schemas with proper relationships and constraints\n- Infer types from schema definitions\n- Write repository-style helpers to isolate queries\n- Implement proper migrations\n\n### Data Access Patterns\n\n- Keep database queries in dedicated modules\n- Avoid N+1 queries; use joins and CTEs\n- Implement pagination for list endpoints\n- Use select projections to limit payload size\n\n## Authentication &amp; Authorization\n\n- Implement server-side auth checks\n- Never trust client-side auth flags\n- Use middleware for route protection\n- Store user data securely with proper encryption\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit Testing (Vitest)\n\n- **Never mock internal code** - only mock external dependencies\n- Use MSW for API mocking when needed\n- Test utilities, repositories, and business logic\n- Mock external services (APIs, databases, file systems)\n\n### Component Testing (React Testing Library)\n\n- Test interactive components with proper accessibility\n- Ensure loading and error states are covered\n- Test user interactions and state changes\n- Use data-testid sparingly; prefer semantic queries\n\n### Integration Testing\n\n- Test API endpoints with real database connections\n- Use test databases with proper cleanup\n- Test authentication flows end-to-end\n- Mock external services consistently\n\n### Test Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Example test structure\ndescribe(\"Feature\", () =&gt; {\n  describe(\"when condition\", () =&gt; {\n    it(\"should expected behavior\", async () =&gt; {\n      // Arrange\n      // Act\n      // Assert\n    });\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Error Handling &amp; Observability\n\n- Implement early returns on invalid input (fail fast)\n- Use typed error codes and messages\n- Log server-side with contextual metadata\n- Never expose stack traces to clients\n- Provide user-friendly error messages\n\n## Security Best Practices\n\n- Validate all inputs at boundaries\n- Use environment variables for sensitive data (server-only)\n- Implement proper CORS policies\n- Sanitize user inputs\n- Use HTTPS in production\n- Implement rate limiting where appropriate",

        "contents": "- Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants\n\n### Constants and Values\n\n- **Always define constants** instead of hardcoding strings, numbers, or values\n- **Use descriptive constant names** that explain the purpose\n- **Group related constants** in dedicated files or objects\n- **Export constants** from centralized locations\n- **Use TypeScript enums** for related constant groups\n- **Define magic numbers** as named constants\n- **Use configuration objects** for complex values\n\n### Functional Programming Patterns\n\n- **Prefer pure functions** - same input always produces same output\n- **Use composition over inheritance** - combine small functions into larger ones\n- **Minimize side effects** - isolate side effects to specific functions\n- **Use higher-order functions** - functions that take or return functions\n- **Favor immutable data** - avoid mutating objects and arrays\n- **Use functional utilities** - map, filter, reduce, pipe, compose\n- **Avoid classes unless necessary** - prefer object literals and functions\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n1. **Analyze requirements** → identify affected layers\n2. **Schema first** (if needed) → update database schema\n3. **Business logic** → implement in server layer\n4. **UI layer** → RSC/client split with proper boundaries\n5. **Testing** → unit, integration, and component tests\n6. **Quality checks** → typecheck, lint, test\n\n## File Generation Patterns\n\nWhen implementing new features, create:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nsrc/\n├─ server/\n│  ├─ api/routers/[feature].ts     # tRPC router composition\n│  ├─ api/procedures/[feature].ts  # Individual tRPC procedures\n│  ├─ services/[feature].ts        # Business logic services\n│  ├─ clients/[service].ts         # External service clients\n│  └─ __tests__/[feature].test.ts\n├─ lib/\n│  ├─ constants.ts                 # Constants and configuration\n│  ├─ schemas.ts                   # Zod schemas\n│  ├─ utils.ts                     # Utility functions\n│  └─ __tests__/[feature].test.ts\n├─ components/[feature]/",

        "contents": "import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\nimport { hasEnvVars } from \"../utils\";\n\nexport async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n\n  // If the env vars are not set, skip proxy check. You can remove this\n  // once you setup the project.\n  if (!hasEnvVars) {\n    return supabaseResponse;\n  }\n\n  // With Fluid compute, don't put this client in a global environment\n  // variable. Always create a new one on each request.\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =&gt;\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n            request,\n          });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n\n  // Do not run code between createServerClient and\n  // supabase.auth.getClaims(). A simple mistake could make it very hard to debug\n  // issues with users being randomly logged out.\n\n  // IMPORTANT: If you remove getClaims() and you use server-side rendering\n  // with the Supabase client, your users may be randomly logged out.\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n  const user = data?.claims;\n\n  // Public routes that don't require authentication\n  const publicRoutes = [\"/\", \"/auth/login\", \"/auth/error\"];\n  const isPublicRoute = publicRoutes.some((route) =&gt;\n    request.nextUrl.pathname === route || request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(route)\n  );\n\n  // If no user and not a public route, redirect to login\n  if (!user &amp;&amp; !isPublicRoute) {\n    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n    url.pathname = \"/auth/login\";\n    return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n  }\n\n  // If user exists, check for verified work email and approval\n  if (user)\n}",

        "contents": "import { cookies } from \"next/headers\";\n\n/**\n * Especially important if using Fluid compute: Don't put this client in a\n * global variable. Always create a new client within each function when using\n * it.\n */\nexport async function createClient() {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies();\n\n  return createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return cookieStore.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          try {\n            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n              cookieStore.set(name, value, options),\n            );\n          } catch {\n            // The &#96;setAll&#96; method was called from a Server Component.\n            // This can be ignored if you have proxy refreshing\n            // user sessions.\n          }\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "export async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {\n\n}\n\nexport const config = {\n  matcher: [\n    /*\n     * Match all request paths except:\n     * - _next/static (static files)\n     * - _next/image (image optimization files)\n     * - favicon.ico (favicon file)\n     * - images - .svg, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp\n     * Feel free to modify this pattern to include more paths.\n     */\n    \"/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp)$).*)\",\n  ],\n};",
        "signatures": {},
